title: Activate the new manifest and workflow version after the cutover suite is green
description:
Final step of the recursive repository-discovery cutover, after the split into tasks 45 to 51.

Every call-site migration now lives in its own task: 45 manifest bootstrap, 46 repositoryBranches, 47 taskGroups, 48 prepareTasks, 49 mergeTaskWorktrees finalization, 50 workflow and SKILL approval split, 51 legacy manifest routing. This task is only the version flip that activates the new manifest and workflow version once all of them have landed.

Flip the version only after the complete end-to-end suite passes: a full node --test tests/ run plus npx tsc --noEmit, both green, in the same commit. Isolate the flip as its own commit so it can be reverted without unwinding the migration.

This task was attempted three times as a single whole-cutover unit and refused each time for a different verified reason: detached-HEAD resolution semantics, discoverRepositoryTree checking out working directories (fixed by task 44), and the absence of any manifest bootstrap (now task 45). Do not re-merge the split steps back into this task.

Tests: the version constant advances only with the full suite green, and a guard refuses the flip on any nonzero exit.

title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.

title: Drive mergeTaskWorktrees through the finalization and publication pipeline
description:
Step 4 of the task 35 cutover split, and its largest behavior change.

Rewire scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts runAsCli to drive scripts/runFinalizer.ts, scripts/runConsolidation.ts, scripts/operationPush.ts, scripts/basePublication.ts and scripts/taskArchival.ts. Read all five in full before editing.

CLI contract decision already made by the user — implement it, do not re-litigate: the script keeps its current front door. It accepts the flat WorkflowArguments JSON as argv[2] and writes the same stdout shape it writes today. Translate the flat arguments into the graph and occurrence shapes INSIDE the script. Every existing test in tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts must keep passing unchanged, with no rewritten CLI assertions. A graph-shaped front door is a later follow-up.

Keep mergeGroupBranchIntoRepo, mergeSubmoduleBranchIntoRepo, resolveGitlinkConflicts and removeWorktreeAndBranch exported and behaviorally unchanged.

Tests: the existing suite passes unedited; the finalization path is exercised end to end against a temporary repository.

title: Split the tackle-tasks workflow into prepare-for-approval and finalize stages
description:
Step 5 of the task 35 cutover split.

Rewire skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js and skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md so preparation returns recursive graph metadata, hook mode, recovery refs, test receipts, review handoffs and readyForApproval instead of immediate merge results, and so the whole-run approval gate runs before finalization.

Use the task 31 modules: scripts/approvalGate.ts, scripts/approvalReadiness.ts and scripts/runAuthorization.ts. There is exactly one approval in a run — do not introduce a second post-merge gate. Replace MERGE_SCHEMA with a shape carrying readyForApproval, and update the SKILL.md flow so the orchestrator presents the gate before anything is finalized or archived.

Tests: the workflow returns readyForApproval rather than merge results before approval; finalization runs only with a valid authorization.

title: Route legacy manifests to a non-destructive refusal with recovery instructions
description:
Step 6 of the task 35 cutover split.

Dispatch legacy versus new manifests through scripts/legacyManifest.ts at the mergeTaskWorktrees.ts runAsCli entry point, routing a legacy manifest to its existing compatible tooling or to a non-destructive refusal that reports exact recovery instructions.

Legacy worktrees must survive the refusal untouched — nothing is removed, reset or force-checked-out on this path.

Tests: a legacy manifest is refused non-destructively, its recovery instructions name the affected worktree, and the worktree still exists on disk afterwards.
